Rashi on Sotah 28a:10:1.hebrew: דידה - דאשה: ידיעה וצוואה ועשייה, כדפרישית:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:10:1.english: Hers - Of the woman: the knowledge, the commanding, and the doing, as I explained.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:12:1.hebrew: ורבי - דלא דריש וו"י, תלתא קראי הוא דכתיבי, וכולהו לדידה: ידיעה ועשייה וצוואה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:12:1.english: And Rabbi - who does not expound the vavs, there are [only] three verses written, and all of them are about her: knowledge, action, and command.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:15:1.hebrew: שלא להוציא לעז - משום דהוא אמר לה בקללה ברישא "את יריכך נופלת" וגו', וסוף המים לבדוק כדרך כניסתן, דכתיב "וצבתה בטנה" והדר "ונפלה יריכה". לכך הוצרך להודיע תחילה שהמים כדרך כניסתן יבדקוה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:15:1.english: So as not to cast aspersions - Because [the kohen] said to her in the curse first, "your thigh shall fall" etc., yet the end of [the process, i.e., the effect of] the water is to examine [her] in the order of their entry [into the body], as it is written "and her belly shall swell" and afterward "and her thigh shall fall." Therefore it was necessary to inform her beforehand that the water will examine her in the order of its entry.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:17:1.hebrew: ואימא כוליה להכי הוא דאתא - לבועל, להודיע דבטן לקה ברישא. מנלן:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:17:1.english: But say that all of it comes for this [purpose] - [that is, that the verse refers] to the paramour, to teach that he was afflicted in the belly first. From where do we know [that it applies to the woman as well]?

Rashi on Sotah 28a:17:2.hebrew: מאי בטן וירך - סתם. הכא והכא דריש ליה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:17:2.english: What is "belly and thigh"? - [The verse states it] without specification [of whose belly or thigh]; both here [regarding her] and there [regarding him], he expounds it.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:19:1.hebrew: שלשה פעמים - "וקינא את אשתו, והיא נטמאה"; "והיתה אם נטמאה"; "תחת אישה, ונטמאה":
Rashi on Sotah 28a:19:1.english: Three times - "And he warned his wife, and she was defiled"; "And it shall be, if she was defiled"; "Under her husband, and she was defiled."

Rashi on Sotah 28a:19:2.hebrew: ואחד לתרומה - שאפילו היא בת כהן ובעלה כהן, נפסלה מן התרומה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:19:2.english: And one for teruma - That even if she is the daughter of a Kohen and her husband is a Kohen, she is disqualified from [eating] teruma.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:1:1.hebrew: דאי אית ביה עון - שבא עליה לאחר שנסתרה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:1:1.english: For if there is sin in him - That he had relations with her after she was secluded.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:1:2.hebrew: בזמן שהאיש מנוקה מעון - שלא בא עליה משנאסרה עליו האשה ההיא, תשא עונה שיבדקוה המים:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:1:2.english: When the man is free of iniquity - That he did not have relations with her after that woman became forbidden to him, [then] she bears her iniquity, [so that] the waters examine her.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:20:1.hebrew: קל וחומר - אינו צריך להביא מן המקרא לפוסלה מן הכהונה מלינשא לכהן, דמקל וחומר אתי:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:20:1.english: A fortiori argument - One does not need to bring [a proof] from the verse to disqualify her from the priesthood, from marrying a priest, for it comes from an a fortiori argument.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:20:2.hebrew: מה גרושה - בת כהן שנתגרשה מישראל וזרע אין לה, שמותרת בתרומה, כדכתיב מלחם אביה תאכל (ויקרא כב) — פסולה לכהונה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:20:2.english: Just as a divorced woman - the daughter of a priest who was divorced from an Israelite and has no offspring, who is permitted to eat terumah, as it is written, "she shall eat of her father's bread" (Leviticus 22) — is [nevertheless] disqualified from the priesthood:

Rashi on Sotah 28a:20:3.hebrew: זו שפסולה מתרומה - מרבויא דנטמאה, כדקאמרת. אינו דין שפסולה לכהונה? ולקמן פריך: והא לא איירי רבי עקיבא בפסול כהונה כלל, דלא אצרכה קרא, ומאי קאמר ליה רבי ישמעאל:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:20:3.english: This [woman] who is disqualified from terumah - [This is derived] from the amplification of [the word] "she was defiled," as you [Rabbi Akiva] say. Is it not logical that she should be disqualified from the priesthood? And below [the Gemara] objects: But Rabbi Akiva does not discuss disqualification from the priesthood at all, for Scripture does not require it [to teach this], so what is Rabbi Yishmael saying to him?

Rashi on Sotah 28a:21:1.hebrew: מה ת"ל והיא נטמאה כו' - גרסינן, ולא גרס א"כ, דמילתא באנפי נפשה היא, ולא נטמאה יתירא קמיבעיא ליה, דהא דרשינן. ולאו רבי ישמעאל לחודיה קאמר לה, אלא סתמא היא, וקראי דעניינא קדריש ואזיל:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:21:1.english: Why does the verse say, "and she was defiled," etc. - We read [it this way], and we do not read "if so," for it is a matter on its own. And he is asking about the superfluous "and she was not defiled," since we do expound it. Rabbi Yishmael is not the only one who says this; rather, it is an anonymous [teaching], and he is expounding the verses of the topic and proceeding [through them].

Rashi on Sotah 28a:21:2.hebrew: מה תלמוד לומר "וקנא את אשתו והיא נטמאה" - דמשמע דודאי נטמאה. ומה תלמוד לומר "או עבר עליו וגו' והיא לא נטמאה"? אי פשיטא ליה דנטמאה, למה שותה? ואי פשיטא דלא נטמאה, למה משקה?:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:21:2.english: Why does the verse say, "And he is jealous of his wife, and she has become defiled" - For it implies that she certainly was defiled. And why does the verse say, "Or if a spirit of jealousy came upon him, etc., and she has not become defiled"? If it is obvious to him that she was defiled, why does she drink? And if it is obvious that she was not defiled, why does he give her to drink?

Rashi on Sotah 28a:21:3.hebrew: מגיד לך הכתוב שעל הספק אסורה - והכי קאמר קרא: אשה זו, שמא נטמאה ושמא לא נטמאה, וקאמר לך דישקנה לברר הספיקא, ואי לא משקה לה — אסורה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:21:3.english: The verse tells you that on account of doubt she is forbidden - And this is what the verse is saying: This woman — perhaps she became defiled and perhaps she did not become defiled — and it tells you that he should give her to drink to resolve the doubt; and if he does not give her to drink, she is forbidden.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:22:1.hebrew: ומכאן אתה - למד ק"ו לשרץ: ספק נגע בטהרות ספק לא נגע, דמחזקינן לה בטומאה מספק:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:22:1.english: And from here you [derive] - Learn a kal vachomer (a fortiori argument) regarding a sheretz (a crawling creature) [in a case where it is] uncertain whether it touched pure foods or did not touch [them], that we presume it to be impure on account of the uncertainty.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:22:2.hebrew: סוטה לא עשה בה כו' - דכתיב "והיא לא נתפשה" — אסורה; הא נתפשה — מותרת. והוא הדין לשוגג: אשתו ואשת איש עמו בבית, ונתכוון לאשתו ונזדמנה לו זו, ואף היא שגגה, כסבורה שהוא בעלה:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:22:2.english: A sota, with regard to whom [the Torah] did not make, etc. - For it is written, "and she was not taken" (Numbers 5:13) — [implying that if she was not taken, she is] forbidden; [but] if she was taken, [she is] permitted. And the same applies to one who acted inadvertently: [for example, where] his wife and another man's wife were with him in the house, and he intended [to be with] his wife but this other woman happened to come to him, and she too acted inadvertently, thinking that he was her husband.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:2:1.hebrew: אלא לבועל ליתני - כך בודקין את הבועל בהדיא, כדתני סיפא בהדיא "כך אסורה לבועל", ולא תנא "כך אסורה לו":
Rashi on Sotah 28a:2:1.english: But if [it refers] to the paramour, let it teach - "So too the waters examine the paramour" explicitly, as it teaches explicitly in the latter clause, "so too she is forbidden to the paramour," and it did not teach "so too she is forbidden to him."

Rashi on Sotah 28a:4:1.hebrew: באו ובאו קאמר - מרבויא דוי"ו, או "ובאו ובאו" הכפולים בפרשה דריש:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:4:1.english: Does he say "they came" and "they came"? - [Does he derive it] from the extra *vav*, or does he expound the doubled "and they shall come… and they shall come" in the passage?

Rashi on Sotah 28a:5:1.hebrew: שנאמר נטמאה ונטמאה - שמע מינה: רבי עקיבא, "וי"ו" דריש:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:5:1.english: As it is stated: "She was defiled" and "and she was defiled" - Learn from this that Rabbi Akiva expounds the letter *vav* [as an addition].

Rashi on Sotah 28a:6:1.hebrew: ועדיין - בהא גופא מיבעיא לי: "נטמאה" "ונטמאה" דריש מרבויא וו"י, או חד "נטמאה" וחד "ונטמאה" קדריש:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:6:1.english: And still - On this very point I have a question: does he expound "nitma'ah" and "v'nitma'ah" from the amplification of vav-vav-yod, or does he expound one "nitma'ah" and one "v'nitma'ah"?

Rashi on Sotah 28a:8:1.hebrew: שיתא קראי - שלשה ובאו כתובים שם: ובאו המים המאררים האלה במעיך לצבות בטן, להודיע לנו דבטן והדר ירך, שלא להוציא לעז, כדאמרי' בפ"ק (לעיל סוטה ט:). וחד והשקה את האשה את מי המרים המאררים ובאו בה המים וגו' — לצואה, שהקב"ה גוזר שיבואו בה המים למרים. וחד לעשייה: והשקה את המים והיתה אם נטמאה וגו' — לעשייה. כאן הודיע הכתוב את ישראל דמבטיח להן שיבדקוה המים. ובכולם כתיב וו"י יתירי, הרי שית:
Rashi on Sotah 28a:8:1.english: Six verses - Three [instances of] "and they shall come" are written there. [One is:] "And these cursed waters shall enter your bowels to cause the belly to swell" — to inform us that [the order is] the belly first and then the thigh, so as not to give rise to a slander, as we say in the first chapter (above, Sotah 9b). And one is: "And he shall make the woman drink the bitter, cursing waters, and the waters shall enter into her etc." — this is for the command, [teaching] that the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees that the waters will enter her as bitter [waters]. And one is for the performance: "And he shall make her drink the water, and it shall be, if she was defiled etc." — for the performance. Here Scripture informed Israel that He promises them that the waters will test her. And in all of them an extra vav-yod is written. Behold, [that makes] six.

Rashi on Sotah 28a:9:1.english: His own - That of the paramour.

Tosafot on Sotah 28a:15:1.hebrew: ההוא דמודע לה כהן - פירוש: הכהן צריך להודיע, שלא להוציא לעז. וכיון דגלי לן קרא דהוא נבדק כמותה, וכתיב בה צואה, ידיעה ועשייה — לא צריך למכתב תו ביה:
Tosafot on Sotah 28a:15:1.english: That the priest informs her - Explanation: The priest must give notice [to him as well], so as not to cause a bad rumor to be spread. And since the verse has revealed to us that he is examined just as she is, and with regard to her there is written commanding, notification, and performance, there is no need for the verse to write [these] again with regard to him:

Tosafot on Sotah 28a:20:1.hebrew: זו שאסורה בתרומה אינה דין שאסורה לכהונה - וליכא למימר: בת ישראל יוכיח, שאסורה בתרומה ומותרת לכהונה. דה"פ: ומה גרושה שמותרת לתרומה, אסורה לכהונה ע"י מעשה שנעשה בה, דהיינו גירושין; זו וכו' אינו דין שאסורה לכהונה ע"י זנות שנעשה בה? אבל בת ישראל, מה שפסולה בתרומה אינו ע"י מעשה. ועוד, אם תנשא בת ישראל לכהן תהא מותרת לתרומה, מה שאין כן באלו שאין להם היתר לעולם. בספרי מתני הכי: ומה גרושה קלה, שמותרת לחזור למגרשה בישראל, פסולה מן הכהונה — סוטה חמורה, דין הוא שפסולה מן הכהונה:
Tosafot on Sotah 28a:20:1.english: "This one, who is forbidden to eat terumah — is it not logical that she is forbidden to the priesthood?" - And one cannot say, "Let a daughter of an Israelite prove otherwise, for she is forbidden to eat terumah yet permitted to the priesthood." For this is what [the baraita] means: Just as a divorcee, who is permitted to eat terumah, is forbidden to the priesthood through an act that was done to her, namely divorce — this one, etc., is it not logical that she is forbidden to the priesthood through the licentiousness that was done with her? But a daughter of an Israelite, her being unfit for terumah is not through any act. Furthermore, if a daughter of an Israelite marries a priest, she becomes permitted to eat terumah, which is not so with these [women], who have no permission ever. In the books of the Mishnah it reads thus: "Just as a divorcee, who is lightly [regarded], who is permitted to return to the man who divorced her if he is an Israelite, is disqualified from the priesthood — a sotah, who is more severe, it is logical that she is disqualified from the priesthood."

Tosafot on Sotah 28a:21:1.hebrew: מה ת"ל היא נטמאה וכו' - כגירסת רש"י. וכך סיומא: "ללמדך שלעולם אין משקין אלא על הספק". וא"ת: וכי איצטריך קרא למיסר ספיקא? יש לומר: הכתוב אוסרה קודם שתיה כאילו היא ודאי. ואע"ג דליכא מלקות, כדמוכח בפ"ק דיבמות (דף יא:), מיהו לאו הבא מכלל עשה איכא. ואפי' אם היא טהורה, נענש בב"ד של מעלה אם בא עליה, כמו על חייבי עשה; ולא כשאר ספיקות, כגון ספק חלב ספק שומן ואכלו, ונודע שהוא שומן — אע"ג דצריך כפרה וסליחה, מיהו לא חמיר כחייבי עשה:
Tosafot on Sotah 28a:21:1.english: "Why does the verse say 'and she has become defiled,' etc." - [This follows] Rashi's reading. And this is its conclusion: "to teach you that one never gives [the water] to drink except in a case of doubt." And if you ask: Was a verse really needed to prohibit a case of doubt? One can say: The verse prohibits her before she drinks, as if she were certainly [defiled]. And although there is no lashing [for this], as is proven in the first chapter of Yevamot (11b), nevertheless there is a prohibition derived from [the implication of] a positive commandment. And even if she is pure, [the man] is punished by the heavenly court if he has relations with her, just as with those liable for violating a positive commandment; but [this is] not like other cases of doubt, such as a doubt whether [the fat] was forbidden fat (chelev) or permitted fat (shuman), and he ate it and it became known that it was permitted fat — although [he] requires atonement and forgiveness, nevertheless it is not as severe as [the case of] those liable for violating a positive commandment:

Tosafot on Sotah 28a:22:1.hebrew: אינו דין שעשה בו ספק כודאי - ליכא למיפרך: נזיר ועושה פסח יוכיחו, שעשה בהן אונס כרצון, דנפקא לן מ"כי ימות מת עליו בפתע פתאום" בספרי ובפרק ב' דכריתות (דף ט.). ואפ"ה לא עשה בהן ספק טומאת התהום כודאי, לפי שטומאת התהום הלכה הוא, ולא סתרינן ק"ו מהלכה. וה"ה דאין להוכיח משם, דהכי אמר בהוכחה: "אף אני אביא זה", והלא אין ללמוד הימנו. אבל הא איכא למתמה: אמאי לא פרכינן "מה לסוטה שכן רגלים לדבר", שהרי קינא לה ונסתרה, כדפרכינן לעיל בריש פ"ק (סוטה דף ב:)? ואין לומר משום דלעיל מיירי בטומאה דבתר קינוי וסתירה דמהימן עד א', התם ודאי איכא רגלים, אבל הכא ילפינן מסתירה דבתר קנויא גרידא, דליכא למיפרך "שכן קינא לה", דקנויא לא חשיב רגלים בלא סתירה. דהא בריש מסכת נדה (דף ב:) דמייתי התם: מקוה שנמדד ונמצא חסר, כל הטהרות שנעשו על גביו, בין ברה"ר בין ברה"י, טמא; ר"ש אומר: ברה"ר טהור, ברה"י תולין. ושניהם לא למדוה אלא מסוטה. רבנן סברי כסוטה: מה סוטה ספק הוא ועשאוה כודאי, אף כו'. ופריך: אי מסוטה, נימא: מה סוטה ברה"י טמא ודאי, הכא נמי טמא ודאי? הכי השתא! התם יש רגלים לדבר, שהרי קנא לה ונסתרה; הכא מאי רגלים לדבר איכא? אלמא אע"ג דמסתירה דבתר קנויא יליף, כי הכא פריך, והכא אמאי לא פריך הכי? ויש לומר: דסתירה על ידי קנויא בסוטה הוי כספק מגע שרץ, שהרי בלא קנויא לא היה שום ספק בסתירה גרידא, דלא נחשדו על העריות; הלכך הקנויא גורם הספק. וה"פ במס' נדה: התם גבי סוטה וספק שרץ, הרי ריעותא, דהיינו השרץ והבועל, קמן אצל הטהרות והאשה; אבל גבי מקוה קודם טבילה, לא ראינו שום ריעותא דאיכא לספוקי על ידה. ולעיל בפ"ק, קודם העדאת עדים, לא הואי שום ריעותא:
Tosafot on Sotah 28a:22:1.english: "Is it not logical that [the Torah] treated a doubt in it like a certainty" - One cannot refute [this] by saying: a nazirite and one who offers the Pesach will prove [otherwise], for with them [the Torah] treated an unavoidable circumstance like a deliberate act, as we derive from "If a man dies beside him suddenly, unexpectedly" (Numbers 6:9), in the Sifrei and in the second chapter of Keritot (9a). And nevertheless, with them [the Torah] did not treat a doubt of the defilement of the depths as a certainty, because the defilement of the depths is a halakhah [transmitted to Moses at Sinai], and we do not undermine a kal vachomer with a halakhah. And likewise one cannot bring proof from there, for the argument is stated thus in the proof: "I too will bring this," but surely one cannot learn from it. But there is something here to wonder about: why do we not refute [the argument] by saying, "What is true of a sotah is that there are grounds for suspicion, since [her husband] warned her and she secluded herself," as we refuted above at the beginning of the first chapter (Sotah 2b)? And one cannot say that [the reason] is that above [the Gemara] was speaking of defilement after warning and seclusion, where one witness is believed, so there certainly are grounds for suspicion there, whereas here we are deriving from seclusion after warning alone, so that one cannot refute [by saying] "since he warned her," because a warning without seclusion is not considered grounds for suspicion. For at the beginning of tractate Niddah (2b), where [the Gemara] cites: [In the case of] a mikveh that was measured and found lacking, all the pure foods that were prepared on its basis, whether in the public domain or in a private domain, are impure; Rabbi Shimon says: In the public domain they are pure, [and] in a private domain we suspend [judgment]. And both of them learned it only from a sotah. The Rabbis hold [that it is] like a sotah: just as a sotah is a doubt and they treated it as a certainty, so too etc. And [the Gemara] asks: If [we learn] from a sotah, let us say: just as a sotah in a private domain is definitely impure, here too it is definitely impure? How can you compare! There there are grounds for suspicion, since he warned her and she secluded herself; here, what grounds for suspicion are there? Evidently, even though [the Gemara] derives from seclusion after warning, it refutes there in this way, so why here does it not refute in this way? And one can answer that seclusion by means of a warning in the case of a sotah is like a doubt of contact with a creeping creature, for without the warning there would be no doubt at all about seclusion alone, since [people] are not suspected of forbidden relations. Therefore the warning creates the doubt. And this is the meaning [of the passage] in tractate Niddah: There, in the case of a sotah and a doubt about a creeping creature, there is a defect, namely the creeping creature and the paramour are before us, next to the pure foods and the woman; but in the case of a mikveh before immersion, we saw no defect on account of which there is room to doubt it. And above, in the first chapter, before the witnesses testified, there was no defect at all.
